title: Heatwave breaks the cold chain
body:
A 46°C heatwave hits North India. Your cold chain fails in 3 cities: 18% of this week's stock spoils and 2,400 customers post complaints. Refunds cost Rs 41 lakh.

The twist: The heatwave is forecast to last 10 more days, and a rival offers to rent you its cold storage at 3× the normal rate.

Your plan must decide: Rent it, ration what you sell, or pause the hottest cities, and the cost of each for the 10 days.

title: A giant gives it away free
body:
A quick-commerce giant launches a free version of your core product or service for its partners. 22% of your customers say they will switch within a month.

The twist: The same giant offers to buy your company at your current price. Your investors are split.

Your plan must decide: Sell, partner, or fight, with what each means for customers and the share price.

title: Fake sustainability data
body:
A journalist shows that a key supplier faked its 'plastic-free' and 'organic' data, which you printed on your packs. #Greenwashing trends with your name in it.

The twist: You find that a second supplier may also be faking data, but checking it takes 6 weeks.

Your plan must decide: Say so now, or wait until you are sure. Who is told, and when.

title: Raw materials up 30%
body:
Palm oil, packaging and fuel costs rise 30% in a quarter. Your gross margin falls from 34% to 21%, and your next funding round is now in doubt.

The twist: Your biggest retailer says it will delist you if your price goes up by more than 5%.

Your plan must decide: Raise prices and risk the retailer, shrink packs, or absorb the cost. Show the margin and cash under your choice.

title: The data feed goes dark
body:
A failure at a national air-navigation data centre cuts the live air-traffic feed your product depends on for 9 hours, on the busiest travel day of the season. 31,000 passengers' flights are disrupted and your customers see stale or missing data.

The twist: Airlines blame your product for slowing their recovery, although the feed failure was not yours. A news channel repeats it.

Your plan must decide: Prove it was not you, or help first and argue later, and what backup data you add so it cannot happen again.

title: The provider builds its own
body:
The national air-navigation provider launches a free analytics dashboard, built on the same air-traffic data you use, for every airline and airport. 30% of your users say they will switch within a quarter.

The twist: The provider offers you a contract to run its dashboard: your product, their brand, a fixed fee, and no access to your users.

Your plan must decide: Sign it, refuse it, or win the customers the free tool does not serve, with the revenue of each over a year.

title: A late alert under investigation
body:
On the day a drone and a training aircraft came too close near a busy airport, an alert from your product reached users late. No one is hurt, but the regulator opens an investigation and the video trends nationwide. Bookings fall 35%.

The twist: Your engineers find that a 4-minute data delay inside your system was never reported to customers.

Your plan must decide: Disclose the delay or not, and what you change in monitoring and safety before the regulator rules.

title: Jet fuel up 35%
body:
Jet fuel prices rise 35% in a month. Airlines, your customers or partners, cut spending on new projects by a quarter and delay paying your invoices by 60 days.

The twist: A lender offers you a loan against your unpaid invoices at 18% interest.

Your plan must decide: Borrow, cut costs, or ask customers to pay early for a discount. Show the cash runway of your choice.

title: The digital identity breach
body:
A premium lifestyle platform you depend on is breached: the purchase histories and private profiles of 40,000 high-net-worth clients leak. Several cancel their memberships and the press names your brand.

The twist: The hackers email 300 of your top clients offering to delete their data for a fee, and two of them ask you to pay it.

Your plan must decide: Pay, refuse, or call the police, and what you say to the 300 within 24 hours.

title: The experience economy disruption
body:
A disruptive startup offers ultra-personalised premium experiences without ownership. 20% of your clients shift spending to it within a quarter and engagement with your products falls.

The twist: The rival offers your three best artisans double pay to design for it. One has already said yes.

Your plan must decide: Match the offer, let them go, or partner with the rival, with the cost of each.

title: The counterfeit revolution
body:
Hyper-realistic counterfeits made with advanced manufacturing flood the market. Even experts cannot tell them apart; resale prices of authentic pieces fall 30% and returns from buyers who fear fakes rise 4×.

The twist: A celebrity posts that her bag from you is a fake. It is genuine, but the post has 2 million likes.

Your plan must decide: Prove it publicly or settle it privately, and how you protect every other client's trust.

title: The luxury market crash
body:
A sudden downturn cuts discretionary spending: luxury retail falls 18%, high-end hospitality bookings 25% and luxury real estate deals 30%. Your next funding round is postponed.

The twist: Your largest investor asks you to cut prices 20% to keep sales up. Your brand team says that would end the brand.

Your plan must decide: Discount, hold prices and cut costs, or launch something cheaper under another name. Show the runway.
